name: Inverted Row with Feet on Swiss Ball
description: The inverted row with feet elevated on a Swiss ball combines horizontal pulling with continuous lower-body stability demand. The unstable foot surface requires constant hip extension and core engagement to prevent the ball from rolling, increasing total muscle recruitment compared to feet-on-floor versions while also training posterior chain co-activation.

execution.starting_position: Grip a fixed bar with both hands and walk the feet onto a Swiss ball. Extend hips to form a plank, arms extended toward the bar.
execution.setup_instructions: Ensure the bar is at an appropriate height relative to the ball — experiment to find the right position for the desired difficulty. Use a bar slightly narrower than shoulder width.
steps: Step 1: Establish the starting plank position with feet centered on the ball.
Step 2: Brace core and squeeze glutes to stabilize the ball.
Step 3: Row the chest to the bar, driving elbows back.
Step 4: At the top, hold 1 second while maintaining ball control.
Step 5: Lower under control to starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop as fatigue sets in
Feet sliding on the ball — press the calves firmly into the surface
Rushing the rep to avoid the balance challenge
safety_considerations: Ensure the ball is properly inflated and rated for body weight
Have the bar set low enough that a fall from the ball does not cause injury
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to chest touching or near bar.
coaching_cues: Press your calves into the ball to control it
Hips stay high — do not let them drop
